四级汇总词汇 · 05英文原文

The Shortcut That Needed a Crossing

需要一处过街点的近路 · 650 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A new bus route was meant to shorten the urban commute. It allowed twenty minutes from a suburban station to the metro platform. For some people the transfer worked. For others, the most direct sidewalk ended at a freeway junction. Jia arrived late three Tuesdays in a row. The cause was not evident at first. Her father blamed a traffic jam on the motorway. She showed him the crowded ramp. The primary delay was crossing an intersection on foot. An extended ride on the expressway would make no difference to that portion of the trip.

2They could detour through a parking lot beside a mall. Drivers reversed there, and an escalator closed early. Another shortcut followed a canal to a narrow tunnel. A pedestrian met a bicycle, a motorbike, and a skateboard in less than a minute. Jia marked both routes on a map. A bus that rolled backward would block the first. A commuter who had ridden a mile still needed a safe link onward. Adding another carriage could accommodate more passengers. It could not give them a usable path between stations.

3At a planning meeting an official called the problem incidental. An ambitious infrastructure undertaking would build a bypass, fund modernization of a railroad spur, and improve the skyline on the outskirts. Its strategic aim was to reduce congestion in the most populous district. Jia showed a lorry pass the last crosswalk and people squeeze along the verge. A careless driver mounted the pavement. The principal asked for a feasible interim measure. Better integration would need coordination between the road crew and the station as well as new construction.

4The roads team considered closing a secondary lane. A delivery cab and a trailer would still need to turn into the driveway. An engineer drew a one-way loop around a small roundabout to keep them apart from walkers. It would also stop a speeding motorcycle from taking the crossing as a shortcut. The team painted a temporary strip across the road and put up a low barrier. The first implementation test would last a week. If a driver had to brake sharply or turn backwards, they would move the line.

5On the first morning a van stopped beside the strip and blocked the view. Jia asked the driver why he had parked there. He needed to unload at the shopping district before eight o'clock. The municipality gave him a loading space near the dock rather than extend the ban to the whole avenue. The crew moved a sign that blocked the ramp for a parent with a stroller. They added a QR code to the sign so commuters could report which route they had actually used.

6A surveyor checked the link to the bus stop. With the lift out, people who could not use the stair took the central street by an old trolley track. Jia drew the linkage, and a crew cleared its ramp.

7By Friday the bus could connect with the tram on time. Some riders still missed the metro when a minor stoppage held up the train. The new crossing could not fix the whole transit system, but it gave people an alternative to the highway ramp. A gradual change in the timetable made the transfers more dependable. The local township proposed a partnership to keep the route clear after flooding. Jia asked them to measure punctuality for walkers as well as for drivers.

8Her father took the new shortcut on Tuesday. A tram rang its bell behind the tower. A child on a scooter waited with a commuter who had driven the old trunk road. A shopkeeper proposed an ambitious expansion of the crossing. Jia asked which direction actually needed more space. The municipality and the station had made a concerted effort to open one link. The next survey would begin there, with the people who needed an efficient route rather than another long detour.

四级汇总词汇 · 05中文译文

需要一处过街点的近路

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一条新公交线路原本能缩短进城通勤，从郊区车站到地铁站台预留了二十分钟。有人能赶上车，可也有人沿着最直接的人行道走，最后却走到高速路匝道口。佳连续三个星期二迟到，起初看不出缘由。父亲怪高速公路堵车，她便带他去看拥挤的匝道。耽搁最久的是徒步过一个路口，在快速路上坐再久一点也解决不了。

2他们可以绕进商场旁的停车场，但有车倒出来，商场的扶梯也关得早。另一条近路沿运河通往窄隧道。行人不到一分钟就碰上一辆自行车、一辆摩托车和一块滑板。佳在图上画出两条路。公交只要向后滑一点，就可能堵住第一条。通勤的人已经坐了一英里，下车后还需要一段安全的路。多挂一节车厢能装更多人，站与站之间的步行路却仍要解决。

3规划会上，有人把它当成小问题。一个大项目打算修绕城路，出钱改造铁路支线，还要改善城郊天际线。战略目标是给人口最多的地区疏堵。佳放给大家看，有辆卡车开过最后一道斑马线，人群只能沿路边挤过去，还有司机为了避队踩上人行道。校长问能不能先做个可行的临时改动。衔接得好不好，需要道路队与车站协调，也需要适当施工。

4道路队考虑封掉一条次要车道，但送货车和拖车仍得转进车道。工程师绕小环岛画了单行线，把车辆与行人分开，也防止飞驰的摩托把行人过街处当近道。工人画了临时过街线，放了一道矮栏。初次试行一周，若有司机必须急刹或倒车，他们就挪线。

5试行第一天，一辆厢式车停在过街线旁挡住视线。佳问司机为什么停在这儿。他得在八点前到商业区卸货。市政部门给他在装卸区边上找了个车位，没有禁停整条大道。工人挪走一块妨碍婴儿车过坡道的牌子，还加上二维码，让通勤者反馈实际走过哪一条路。

6勘测员接着检查到公交站的接驳。电梯坏了，不能走台阶的人就沿旧有轨电车轨道旁的主街过去。佳把接驳路线画出来，工人把坡道清理通畅。

7周五，公交已经能准时接上有轨电车。偶尔停运时，有人还是会错过地铁。新过街点无法修好整套公交系统，却给行人多了一个避开高速匝道的选择。时刻表逐步调整，换乘也更稳定。地方镇政府提议合作，在涨水后保持道路通畅。佳请他们统计司机准不准时，也看看行人是否来得及。

8星期二，父亲和佳走了新近路。车站塔后响起电车铃。一名踩滑板车的孩子和一位开过旧干道的通勤者一起等。店主提议把过街处扩得更大，佳先问，哪个方向确实需要更多地方。市政和车站协力开通了这一处接驳。下次调查就从这里开始，先听听需要一条有效率的路的人怎么说。
